newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania BCR lifts short-term deposit rates again.
newsitem.headline: Romania BCR lifts short-term deposit rates again.

text.p: Romanian state-owned bank Banca Comerciala Romana SA (BCR) said on Tuesday it would raise short-term interest rates for the fourth time this year to protect depositors against quickening inflation in the months ahead.
The bank's rates on individuals' one-month deposits will rise 10 percentage points to an annual 120 percent on Wednesday, a BCR statement said.
Three-month deposits rates will rise to 125 percent from 111 percent, but sight-deposit rates will stay flat at an annual 25 percent.
The move follows similar decisions by most Romanian commercial banks after the central bank (BNR) tightened monetary policy to fight surging inflation.
Last week, the BNR's one-week refinancing funds rate surged to 426.50 percent from 226.35 percent. The jump sent the Lombard rate up to an annual 682.4 percent from a previous 362.16.

January year-on-year inflation rose sharply to 76.3 percent from December's 56.9 percent, and inflation is expected to continue gaining in coming months following the freeing of fuel, electricity and food prices.
The BCR said six-month, nine-months and one-year deposit rates were unchanged at 112 percent, 113 percent and 115 percent, respectively.
